question: Comparing the unilateral (1 tail) and bilateral hypothesis tests (2 tails):

options.opa: Bilateral tests always give higher p values.
options.opb: Bilateral tests always give lower p values.
options.opc: If a unilateral test is significant, so will the bilateral test.
options.opd: A bilateral test is more sensitive than a unilateral test.

analysis: In hypothesis testing, a unilateral test assesses the probability of observing data in one direction, while a bilateral test assesses both directions. A bilateral test typically has a higher p-value than a unilateral test for the same data because it splits the alpha level across two tails. If a unilateral test is significant, the bilateral test may not be significant because it requires a more stringent criterion. Therefore, option c is correct, as a significant result in a unilateral test implies that the effect is in one direction, which would also be significant in a bilateral test, but not vice versa. Options a and b are incorrect as they misrepresent the relationship between p-values in unilateral and bilateral tests. Option d is also incorrect because a bilateral test is generally less sensitive due to the division of the alpha level across two tails.
